ai.definition: Cognitive Architecture Mirroring refers to AI systems that replicate the decision-making processes of a human leader by creating a digital twin of their heuristics, enabling automated high-level strategy.
ai.howItWorks: The system uses recursive neural networks to analyze and map the value weights and bias patterns inherent in the decision logs of a human leader. This mapping is then used to mimic the leader's decision-making process, allowing for automated strategic decisions that align with the original leader’s thought processes.
ai.problemSolved: It addresses the challenge of automating complex, high-level decision-making tasks typically handled by human executives or experts, ensuring consistency and scalability in critical business strategies without direct human oversight.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing and training recursive neural networks on extensive datasets containing historical decisions made by a human leader. This requires significant computational resources and specialized expertise in AI development.
ai.buildProcess: The build process starts with data collection, followed by the selection of relevant decision logs, then training the recursive neural network models to accurately replicate the decision-making patterns. Finally, the model is fine-tuned based on feedback loops and real-world performance.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the initial investment in computational infrastructure, ongoing maintenance costs for AI models, data labeling expenses, and continuous improvement efforts to adapt to changing business environments.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The technology is expected to transition from lab research to early commercial adoption as more companies seek ways to automate high-level decision-making processes without compromising on the quality of strategic decisions.
ai.regulation: Regulatory oversight will likely focus on ensuring transparency, accountability, and ethical use of AI in executive decision support systems. Compliance with data protection laws and guidelines for responsible AI deployment will be crucial.
ai.risks: Risks include potential biases in training data leading to skewed decision-making, over-reliance on the digital twin potentially ignoring new information or context, and challenges in maintaining model accuracy as business environments evolve.
ai.profitability: Profitability is highly dependent on the specific industry and application. Potential for high returns in sectors like finance, healthcare, and strategic consulting where executive-level decisions have significant financial impact.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may involve integrating more advanced AI techniques such as reinforcement learning to improve model adaptability and real-time decision-making capabilities. Additionally, there could be a focus on enhancing the explainability of these models to build trust among users.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and high computational requirements during initial training phases.

subsystems.name: Decision record
subsystems.role: captures what the person decided, the situation they faced and what happened next.

subsystems.name: Context encoder
subsystems.role: turns messy, unstructured situations into a structured state the model can compare.

subsystems.name: Value and preference model
subsystems.role: estimates how much weight the person puts on competing goals — speed versus safety, cost versus reputation.

subsystems.name: Decision policy
subsystems.role: proposes an action when a comparable new situation arrives.

subsystems.name: Validation and audit layer
subsystems.role: checks the model against decisions it has never seen and flags weak calls.

subsystems.name: Human review interface
subsystems.role: shows the recommendation with its reasons so a person can accept, edit or reject it.

buildSteps.title: Collect decision records
buildSteps.detail: With consent and governance, assemble years of past decisions with the context available at the time and what followed.

buildSteps.title: Normalise into cases
buildSteps.detail: Each record is structured as: situation, options on the table, choice made, stated reasoning, later outcome.

buildSteps.title: Learn preferences
buildSteps.detail: Train a model to rank options the way the person did, using comparisons rather than a single 'correct' answer.

buildSteps.title: Fit a decision policy
buildSteps.detail: Fine-tune a model to reproduce choices, retrieving similar past cases so its reasoning is grounded in real history.

buildSteps.title: Backtest
buildSteps.detail: Replay held-out real decisions and measure agreement — and examine systematically where it disagrees.

buildSteps.title: Add uncertainty and limits
buildSteps.detail: The system abstains or escalates when confidence is low or the decision falls outside an approved category.

buildSteps.title: Deploy narrowly
buildSteps.detail: Start as an advisor on low-stakes, reversible choices that a human still signs off on.

buildSteps.title: Monitor and retrain
buildSteps.detail: Track drift and disagreement, and update the model as the person's judgement and the business change.

prerequisites.why: needed to read and reason over unstructured business context — documents, messages and meetings.

prerequisites.tech: Preference learning and reinforcement learning from human feedback
prerequisites.why: the established machinery for turning human comparisons into a usable value model.
a person's judgement depends on years of accumulated context that must be recalled accurately.
the consequences of strategic decisions unfold over years and are rarely recorded in a form a model can learn from.
separating a person's policy from the circumstances they happened to face is the core statistical difficulty.

pathway.milestone: assistants that draft, summarise and search in one person's style using their own documents
pathway.unlocks: productivity gains without any claim of copying judgement.

pathway.milestone: advisory models that predict a specific leader's likely call on bounded, repeatable decisions, with human sign-off
pathway.unlocks: a useful check on bias and consistency, if accuracy is honestly measured.

pathway.milestone: scenario and training simulators that ask 'what would this person do here?' with explicit uncertainty
pathway.unlocks: faster succession and onboarding, and stress-testing strategy before committing.

pathway.milestone: narrowly delegated decisions in well-bounded domains under audit
pathway.unlocks: limited autonomy — full automation of executive strategy is unlikely, because goals, context and stakes keep changing.
